title: My Job
subtitle: Emma has worked at the coffee shop for six years. This is what the job is really like.
description: An A1 reading and listening text about a simple job: what you do all day, the people you work with, and what is good and bad about it.
source: authored for this site; no source document
passage: I work at a coffee shop. I am there six days a week, from six in the morning to two in the afternoon.
My job is not difficult, but it is not easy either. I stand all day. I make coffee, I take orders, I clean the tables, and I talk to a lot of people.
I work with Carlos. He is twenty-three and he is a student, so he works in the afternoon. My boss, Ray, opens the shop with me on Saturday.
Some of our customers are regular. A woman comes every morning at seven for the same thing: a large coffee, no sugar. I know her face, but I don't know her name.
The money is not good. But I like the mornings, I like the people, and at two o'clock I am free.
Jack says I should look for a better job. Maybe. But not this year.

exercises.title: Understanding the Text
exercises.instructions: Read again and choose the best answer.

items.prompt: How many days a week does Emma work?
items.explanation: “I am there six days a week.”

items.prompt: What does Emma say about the work?
options: It is not hard, but it is not easy
items.explanation: “My job is not difficult, but it is not easy either.”

items.prompt: Why does Carlos work in the afternoon?
items.explanation: “He is twenty-three and he is a student.”

options: Somebody who comes again and again
Somebody who pays with a card
items.explanation: The woman “comes every morning at seven for the same thing”.

items.prompt: What does Emma not know about the woman?
items.explanation: “I know her face, but I don't know her name.”

items.prompt: Why does Emma stay in this job?
options: She likes the mornings and the people, and she finishes early
items.explanation: “The money is not good. But I like the mornings, I like the people, and at two o'clock I am free.”

exercises.title: Work Words
exercises.instructions: Choose the word that matches the meaning.

items.prompt: A person who buys something in a shop is a ___.
items.explanation: A customer buys; a boss tells you what to do.

items.prompt: The person who tells you what to do at work is your ___.
items.explanation: Your boss is above you at work.

items.prompt: This exercise is not difficult. It is ___.
items.explanation: Easy is the opposite of difficult.

items.prompt: After two o'clock I have no work. I am ___.
items.explanation: Free means with no work to do.

items.prompt: She comes every day at the same time. She is a ___ customer.
items.explanation: Regular means happening again and again.

exercises.title: Make the Sentence
exercises.instructions: Put the words in the correct order.

discussion: What is your job? What do you do every day?
Do you work with other people? Who?
What is good about your job? What is not good?
What time do you start and finish?
